objective: Test dated company contact, transaction-support vendors, explicit public records and backwards buyer histories.
result: New evidence of multiple actual buyers evaluating HAE assets, including unsuccessful bidders; no PHVS-specific buyer contact or transaction footprint verified.

contact.finding: Search results mostly clinician disclosures and advocacy events. HAEi August2025 describes separate Pharvaris Patient Council participation and virtual meetings with Astria,CSL,Takeda; does not describe PHVS-Takeda bilateral meeting.

vendors.finding: Searched PHVS with named compensation/transaction-communications vendors and general integration/benefits terms. Public disclosure mentions compensation benchmarking for late-stage development, not a named acquisition mandate.
vendors.limitation: Indexed web screen, not private client lists or exhaustive vendor census.

public_records.status: Limited screen; no buyer link found
public_records.finding: Patent co-mentions of Takeda/PHVS arise in citations. US12629363B2 lists Pharvaris GmbH as original/current assignee on Google Patents; this is a secondary-index lead, not legal title verification. Official assignment link failed to load.
public_records.limitation: No exhaustive patent/trademark/company-register audit. No legal ownership conclusion or absence claim.

kalvista.fact: Jefferies engaged18strategic parties including PartyA following pivotal data; outreach is not18bids.
PartyA proposed21USD/share cash; revised22.50July30. Target rejected price.
PartyB and PartyD withdrew because they could not justify even mid20s/share; expressed willingness to re-engage lower if lead transaction failed.
Chiesi signed27USD/share deal; other parties remain anonymized in reviewed background.

astria.fact: Kaken and second unnamed Japanese company submitted Japan licensing term sheets; Kaken negotiations advanced.
Unnamed publicly held biopharma Party1 proposed all-stock merger leaving Astria shareholders35-36% combined ownership.
Astria informed Party1 it had signed exclusivity with another party; BioCryst ultimately acquired Astria.

buyer_histories.interpretation: Sector acquisition demand not limited to winning buyers. Failed parties are plausible buyer-pool hypotheses, not identified PHVS counterparties. Price discipline is meaningful counterevidence to automatic premium. Selected successful deals cannot calibrate unconditional takeover odds.

model_decision: Strengthens qualitative buyer-pool rationale; no numeric probability adjustment, named Takeda inference or valuation change. No per-share cross-company valuation comparison.
method: Targeted public searches across four source families; follow-ups justified by full KalVista/Astria histories; reused prior vendor findings and filings. No agents, private tracking or bulk archive scraping.
next_step: Retain takeover scenario; only extend signal search on a specific new buyer-identifying or PHVS-specific record.
